## Problem

`GET /api/openchamber/message-search` silently widens a scoped search when `role` or `lifecycle` is repeated in the query string. This is the same defect class as #2421 (repeated `session` degraded to `''` and searched every conversation), but the #2421 fix guarded only `session` — the sibling filters still degrade to their widest values.

## Evidence

Schema (`packages/web/server/lib/message-search/routes.ts:26-36`):

```ts
role: z.enum(['user', 'assistant', 'reasoning']).nullable().catch(null),
lifecycle: z.enum(['active', 'archived', 'all']).catch('all'),
```

The route (`:100-103`) rejects a non-string `session` with 400, then parses the rest of the query through the catch-schema (`:104`) and passes the results straight to the runtime (`:107-117`, runtime `runtime.ts:167-178` passes `role`/`lifecycle` through to the engine).

Express delivers a repeated query key as an array, and a zod `.catch()` fires on any parse failure — including wrong-type array input — so:

- `?role=assistant&role=user` → array → catch → `role: null` → searches **all roles**
- `?lifecycle=archived&lifecycle=active` → array → catch → `lifecycle: 'all'` → searches **all lifecycles**

Verified with the repo's zod (4.3.6), same schema shapes as the route:

```js
querySchema.parse({ role: null, ...{ role: ['assistant','user'], lifecycle: ['archived','active'], q: 'x' } })
// → { role: null, lifecycle: 'all' }
```

Note the inconsistency on the adjacent route: `GET /api/openchamber/message-search/sessions` uses `groupedQuerySchema` (`:46-55`, all-optional, no catch), so a repeated param there fails `safeParse` and gets a 400 (`:129-132`). Only the single-search route widens.

## Why it matters

A client, proxy, or copied URL that duplicates one of these keys (the exact trigger shape as #2421, plus the family in #2418/#2419/#2420/#2371) silently gets wider results than requested — e.g. archived conversations included when only active was asked for. The failure is silent: 200 with plausible results.

(`reasoning`/`order`/`before`/`q`/`limit` degrade to their defaults on repeat, which is benign; `directory` explicitly accepts arrays. `role` and `lifecycle` are the two that widen scope.)

## Acceptance criteria

- A repeated (non-string) `role` or `lifecycle` on `GET /api/openchamber/message-search` answers 400, mirroring the `session` guard.
- Regression tests pin it, mirroring the repeated-session test in `routes.test.js:34`.
- Scalar and absent `role`/`lifecycle` keep working as before.

## Suggested shape

Extend the raw `session` guard to `role` and `lifecycle` (any non-string scalar-or-absent check before `querySchema.parse`), so the whole filter set rejects ambiguous repeats instead of catching them to widest.

## What
First-party N-API no-replace directory rename plus loader, packaging, and `/api/fs/rename` wiring:

## Problem

`POST /api/fs/exec` (`packages/web/server/lib/fs/routes.ts`) accepts an unbounded `commands` array and retains every finished job for 30 minutes with no entry cap, so one client can grow server memory far beyond the per-command output cap that #737/#739 put in.

Evidence on `origin/main` `69dcd99fa56fe8f63ee87932759a9c2bdd203d1c`:

- Array length is never checked: `if (!Array.isArray(commands) || commands.length === 0)` (`routes.ts:2199`) — only empty is rejected. The route sits under the `/api/fs` 50 MB JSON body allowance (`core-routes.ts:1193-1241`), so a single request can carry tens of thousands of command strings. `runExecJob` (`routes.ts:932-965`) runs them sequentially and keeps every `CommandResult` (each up to `execOutputMaxBytes`, default 4 MiB, `routes.ts:598`) in `job.results`.
- The job store has no size bound: `const execJobs = new Map<string, ExecJob>()` (`routes.ts:829`) and `pruneExecJobs` (`routes.ts:837-845`) evicts only entries older than `EXEC_JOB_TTL_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000` (`routes.ts:153`), called only on exec POST/GET. There is no `MAX_ENTRIES` eviction. Sibling stores in the same file both cap count: preview grants evict oldest past `PREVIEW_GRANT_MAX_ENTRIES = 256` (`routes.ts:156-175`) and the git read cache evicts past `GIT_READ_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES = 500` / 1 MiB (`routes.ts:329-330, 860-878`).
- Consequence: N requests (or one request with a huge `commands` array) pin up to ~N × commands × 4 MiB of output in memory for 30 minutes. `GET /api/fs/exec/:jobId` even refreshes `updatedAt` (`routes.ts:2292`), extending retention on read.

## Impact

Authenticated local client (the web UI attack surface is any workspace-scoped caller) can exhaust server memory / force long sequential shell execution with a single 50 MB request or a burst of small ones. Prior fixes capped per-command bytes (#737→#739) and kill the process tree (#913→#932), but neither bounds command count or job count, so the DoS vector remains.

## Acceptance criteria / suggested fix

- [ ] Cap `commands.length` per request (e.g. ≤ 32; reject larger with 400/413) in `POST /api/fs/exec`.
- [ ] Cap retained `execJobs` entries (e.g. 256 like preview grants, or 500 like the git cache) with oldest-first eviction on insert, independent of the 30-minute TTL.
- [ ] Cap total retained `job.results` bytes (or per-job command count × output cap) so worst-case retention is bounded; alternatively store results behind the same byte budget as the git read cache.
- [ ] Add regression tests: oversized `commands` array rejected; job-store eviction drops oldest past the cap; TTL prune still works.
- [ ] Confirm existing exec tests (`routes.test.js` exec block, incl. background-rejection and git-cache tests) still pass.

## Dedupe notes

Searched open/closed issues and open PRs for `execJobs`, `exec job`, `commands array`, `/api/fs/exec`. Found the per-command output family (#737 CLOSED via #739, #741 CLOSED, #913 CLOSED via #932, #1567/#1590 decode fixes) — all bound bytes per command or process lifetime, none bounds command count or retained job count. No open tracker or open PR covers this.

## Decision (Drew, 2026-11-23, on #152)

Agents may write setup commands and project actions in OpenChamber. PR #179 shipped `projects.setup` read-only because those commands run outside OpenCode's permission rules; Drew's call: allow the writes — setup and project actions are the point of the agent tool, and OpenCode's permission rules still govern execution. The 2026-10-22 adopted default (read-only stays) is superseded by this decision.

## Scope

- Add the write counterpart to `projects.setup`: agents can set/replace a project's setup commands through the openchamber tool, under the same save-lock discipline PR #194 established for project writes.
- Allow agent writes to project actions (create/update/remove), same lock discipline.
- Keep the enterprise-mode posture coherent with the existing rule: in enterprise mode, agent config writes stay closed (2026-10-22 default, not superseded) unless this issue's implementation records otherwise with a reason.
- Writes must be auditable the way other agent-tool mutations are (who/what/when in the action result).

## Acceptance

- An agent can write a project's setup commands and project actions via the tool, and the change is visible in the project configuration and takes effect on the next run of that setup/action.
- Enterprise mode still refuses these writes.
- Tests cover the write path, the lock behaviour, and the enterprise refusal.

Filed from the #152 tracker close-out (task 17623): the decision was that tracker's last open thread; the tracker closes with this issue as the implementation's home.

## Context

Issue #2572 requires `/api/fs/rename` to preserve a concurrently created empty destination directory. `renameWithoutReplace` currently uses `fs.rename` for directory sources. POSIX rename may replace an empty destination directory, and Node does not expose the platform's exclusive-rename flags.

A precheck followed by `rename`, placeholder directory, or copy fallback cannot preserve the source and raced destination inodes atomically. Linux provides `renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE)`, macOS provides `renamex_np(RENAME_EXCL)`, and Windows provides a move without `MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING`. Node and Bun do not expose these operations directly.

## Acceptance criteria

- Add a supported native operation for atomic no-replace directory rename on the app's supported Linux, macOS, and Windows targets.
- Return an existing-path error when a destination appears before commit, leaving both directory paths and inodes unchanged.
- Fail closed when the platform or filesystem cannot provide the exclusive operation. Do not fall back to check-then-rename.
- Keep ordinary directory moves and same-path/case-only renames working.
- Add deterministic race coverage and verify the platform behavior in Linux, macOS, and Windows CI.
- Document native loading and any filesystem or platform constraint.
- Wire the helper into the existing `/api/fs/rename` route and complete issue #2572.

Related: #2572.

body:
## Evidence

Follow-up to #2375. The no-replace rename fix in `packages/web/server/lib/shared/atomic-rename.ts` intentionally keeps plain `rename()` for directory sources (`sourceKind.isDirectory`, lines 51-53); the comment says a directory rename onto an existing file or non-empty directory fails. But POSIX `rename(2)` replaces an existing **empty directory**.

The route's existence check is still separate from commit (`packages/web/server/lib/fs/routes.ts:2059-2079`): if `/api/fs/rename` observes the destination as absent and another process creates an empty directory there before `renameWithoutReplace` commits, the plain directory `rename()` replaces that newly created directory and returns success. A real Node filesystem probe confirmed the primitive: after creating an empty destination directory, `fs.rename(sourceDir, destinationDir)` succeeded and changed the destination inode to the source directory's inode. This is the directory-shaped residual explicitly left by #2375's implementation, not the regular-file race covered by that issue's regression test.

## Why it matters

A concurrent directory creation can be silently discarded, and callers receive success rather than the existing 409 conflict. The route promises not to overwrite a distinct destination; the no-replace behavior currently does not hold for this valid directory edge case.

## Acceptance criteria

- If a distinct empty destination directory appears after the route's lookup but before commit, return the existing 409 `already-exists` response and preserve both source and destination paths/inodes.
- Add a real-filesystem regression that injects empty-directory creation between the destination lookup and commit.
- Keep supported directory moves and same-path/case-only rename behavior working; document/test platform-specific semantics for supported OSes.
title: fix(web): preserve a concurrently created empty directory in /api/fs/rename

## Summary
`GET /api/fs/preview/<grant>/<path>` enforces only lexical containment against `grant.base`, then `realpath`s and serves the canonical target with no canonical re-check — so a symlink inside the granted tree pointing outside the workspace is served with 200, including unauthenticated (the grant token is the credential on this route).

## Evidence
- Mint (`packages/web/server/lib/fs/routes.ts:1589-1613`): canonicalizes the page (`realpath(resolved.resolved)`), mints `{ base: resolved.base /* lexical */, readRoot /* canonical */ }`.
- Serve (`routes.ts:1626-1689`): `resolveWorkspacePath({ baseDirectory: grant.base })` is lexical-only, then `const canonicalPath = await fsPromises.realpath(resolved.resolved)` — but `canonicalPath` is never checked back against `grant.base`/`grant.readRoot`. The only use of `isPathWithinRoot(canonicalPath, grant.readRoot)` (:1674) gates the `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: null` header, not the serve.
- Sibling `POST /api/fs/reveal` (`routes.ts:2091-2098`) does the correct thing: `realpath` both sides and 403s when `!isPathWithinRoot(canonicalTarget, canonicalBase)`. The preview serve route skips this step.
- Live repro (vitest harness minting a grant for `site/index.html`, then `GET /api/fs/preview/<grant>/site/evil.txt` where `evil.txt -> <workspace>/../secret.txt`): **200 with the outside file's bytes** (`EVIL STATUS 200 BODY TOP-SECRET-OUTSIDE-WORKSPACE`). Repro file: `packages/web/server/lib/fs/preview-symlink-repro.test.js` (scratch only, not committed). Expected after fix: 403 (or 400) without serving bytes.

## Impact
Anyone holding/sharing a preview URL (grant-scoped, no session auth on the GET) can read arbitrary files the server process can read by planting or following a symlink inside the previewed tree — e.g. `secret.txt` adjacent to the workspace, or via a symlinked ancestor. The mint route's own canonicalization shows the codebase already treats this as a boundary; the serve route just doesn't re-enforce it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] After `realpath` in the preview serve route, deny (403) when the canonical target is not within the canonical grant root (`grant.readRoot`, mirroring the reveal route's canonical-both-sides check), instead of serving.
- [ ] Regression test: grant rooted in dir A, symlink inside A pointing to a file outside A, asserts the serve returns 403/400 and never the outside bytes (plus a positive test that a normal in-root file still serves).
- [ ] Symlinked-ancestor escape (granted dir itself reached through a symlink pointing out) covered by the same check.

## Dedupe
- OPEN #2458 covers vscode bridge read/stat symlink escapes — different surface (extension bridge, no grant involved).
- CLOSED #1605 is preview-serve byte-cap accounting — different defect on the same route.
- CLOSED #2520 contained the sibling `/api/fs/reveal` route — this issue is the preview-serve route that was left open.
- No open PR touches the preview serve route (only open PR is #2535 ci token fallback).

Follow-ups to the model-pool settings rebuild. Everything listed here is open; nothing in it blocks the merged work.

Merged so far: #2469 (rebuild), #2486 (model defaults and lock, OpenCode model settings), #2489 (fixes found in a real browser), #2492 (last-model wait), #2493 (effort fixes for pools of pools), #2497 (docs: a pool moves on after a failure that follows output). OpenCode side: developing-today-forks/opencode#2674, #2676, #2679.

## 1. "Try the next pool model" takes the session off the pool (needs a decision)

After the button retries a reply, the chat box shows the member it used (for example `mock/okay`) instead of the pool, and the next message goes straight to that model. From then on the session has no failover until the pool is picked again.

- Seen in a browser on 2026-11-22: after the click, the composer read "Current model: mock/okay", and the next pick had to start from `okay`.
- Cause: `retryMessage` (`packages/ui/src/sync/session-ui-store.ts`) resends the prompt through `sendMessage` with the chosen model, and a send makes that model the session's model.
- Choices: keep it, or retry with the member once and keep the session on the pool. The pool-member pin (#2482, OpenCode #2672, both merged) already keeps a session on the pool with one member preferred, so the button could reuse it. That needs an installed OpenCode with #2672.
- My recommendation is the second. It is a product decision, so it is not built. #2126 is where the original ask lives ("configurable whether it force-stops or applies on the next message").

## Gap — paired clients have no route scopes and no programmatic client kind

Found during the babysitter enrollment for developing-today/code#1271
(fleet queue task 16620, 2026-11-14): enrolling a paired OpenChamber
client named `babysitter-sandbox` for a sandbox babysitter process
(sandbox -> laptop :3000). The enrollment and all five babysitter
routes verified live, but two parts of the requested design are not
expressible in the current client-auth model:

1. **No route scopes.** `lib/client-auth/remote-clients.js` issues an
   unscoped bearer token (`oc_client_...`); a paired client can call
   every route its token authenticates, not a named subset. The
   babysitter design (code#1271) asked for a client scoped to five
   routes: session reads, session-activity, quota reads, message
   injection, plan/todo binding reads. There is no field on the client
   record, the pairing session, or the redeem call to declare or
   enforce that subset.
2. **No programmatic client kind.** Pairing restricts kinds to
   `mobile | desktop` (`VALID_CLIENT_KINDS` in
   `lib/client-auth/pairing.js`; redeem normalizes anything else to
   `mobile`). A headless babysitter had to enroll as kind `desktop`
   to be represented truthfully-ish in the device list.

Related observation from the same verification: the client-management
route's own-record scoping works as designed (with the babysitter
token, `GET /api/client-auth/clients` returned only its own record),
but requests arriving over the sandbox's trusted tunnel transport are
also session-trusted without a token, so on that transport the token
is not the operative credential. Worth a deliberate decision when
scopes are designed: scope enforcement should bind to the token, not
to the transport's trust.

Ask: add an optional `scopes` set on paired clients (route families,
enforced where client auth is resolved), and a `programmatic` (or
`service`) client kind allowed in pairing. Until then, paired-client
enrollments for automation are necessarily unscoped — documented in
the #1188 inventory (fleet goal workspace,
`openchamber-api-inventory-2026-10-26.md`, babysitter section
2026-11-14) and on code#1271.
title: Paired clients have no route scopes and no programmatic client kind (babysitter enrollment gap, code#1271)

Found while fixing a Codex thread on #216.

When a send of a goal writer job ends without a report, the server releases the job with a reason that says the message may have gone out:

- `RESTART_REASON` in `packages/web/server/lib/session-goal/spec-jobs.js`: "the server restarted while the message was being sent; check the session before sending it again"
- `CLAIM_EXPIRED_REASON` in the same file (new in #216): "the window sending the message did not report back, so it may have been sent; check the session before sending it again"

`GoalSpecJobCard.tsx` shows every send failure under the heading `chat.goal.writer.card.sendFailed`, "The message was not sent.", so the card states both that the message was not sent and that it may have been. A user who reads only the heading can send it a second time.

Fix shape: the job says when the outcome is unknown (an optional field such as `sendUncertain`, set by those two releases and kept in the jobs file), and the card shows a heading such as "The message may have been sent." for it, in all 15 locales. A job without the field keeps today's heading, so older files and servers read as before.

Because deletion only clears the current session when it still matches the deleted ID, the newly selected session remains valid and is then unexpectedly replaced by this draft; recheck the runtime and current session after deletion before navigating.
>

> <!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

From Codex's review of #216 (https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/pull/216#discussion_r4338000764, `packages/ui/src/components/chat/goalSpecJobEdit.ts`, `replaceEmptySessionWithDraft`).

Back to edit on a new chat's goal writer job removes the empty session and opens a new-session draft for the message. The window is checked before the removal, but if the user switches to another session while `deleteSession` is in flight, `openNewSessionDraft` still runs afterwards and replaces the session they moved to with the draft.

Why it was not fixed in #216: the message needs a home either way. Opening the draft takes over the user's screen, and skipping it leaves the composer edit aimed at a session that was just removed, so the message would sit in `pendingComposerEdits` with no composer to take it. A fix needs a way to hand the message to a new-session draft without showing it, or a decision that the draft should open anyway with a notice.

What done looks like: after the removal, a user who is still on the removed session gets the draft as today; a user who moved elsewhere stays where they are, and the message is still recoverable from a draft or composer they can find.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] After the removal, a user who is still on the removed session gets the draft as today; a user who moved elsewhere stays where they are, and the message is still recoverable from a draft or composer they can find.
- [ ] If the successor goal-edit flow has no delete-then-open-draft sequence, this is met by absence and the issue can be closed as obsolete with that noted.

## What I want

When I pick a model or an effort level by hand (the goal writer, the composer, a pool), OpenChamber should remember that choice and what it was for. Over time those notes should feed the classifier that picks models in Auto mode, and Settings should be able to suggest changes from them.

My words: "automatically track which models are chosen when over time and create notes that can be fed to classifier and used for settings recs. maybe allow settings changes propose and then approve/decline when in single mode in settings ui? over time then a small model would get better because can provide feedback and auto model picker for auto mode would understand user intent a bit better."

## What exists today

- The goal writer can now take a model and effort picked in the goal window (PR for the goal editor rework, branch `feat/goal-editor-rework`). A pick applies to that goal only, unless the user presses Remember or turns on `sessionGoalWriterRememberChoice`.
- `recentModels` and `recentEfforts` in settings record what was picked, but not why or for what.
- `plan_info` notes record what the user says about plans; nothing records choices made in the UI.

## Proposal

1. Record each manual model or effort choice as an event: where it was made (goal writer, composer, pool, Settings), the default it replaced, the session's model, and the length of the input it was for.
2. Summarize the events into short notes, such as "picks low effort on Opus for goal specs", and keep them where the classifier prompt and Settings can read them.
3. In Settings, while a single model is in use, show a proposed change built from the notes, with Approve and Decline. A decline is recorded too.
4. Give those notes to Jev and the small model when they choose a model in Auto mode.

## Open questions

- Where the events are stored and how long they are kept.
- Whether recording is on by default. Recording choices is a privacy question even when it stays local.
- How a proposal is shown without becoming a nag.

Related: route pool descriptions for classification (separate issue).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Manual model/effort choices are recorded as events with surface (goal writer, composer, pool, Settings), the default replaced, the session model, and input length.
- [ ] Events are summarized into short notes readable by the Auto-mode classifier prompt and by Settings.
- [ ] Settings (single-model mode) can propose a change built from the notes with Approve/Decline, and declines are recorded too.
- [ ] The body's open questions (retention/privacy of choice history, note format) are answered or explicitly deferred with a named owner.
title: Learn from manual model and effort choices: notes for the classifier and Settings suggestions

## Problem

Upgrading or restarting OpenChamber can drop OpenCode sessions or change the port. Today this works through detached OpenCode adoption (`state.json`) and optional socket activation (`LISTEN_FDS`). Socket activation still needs a systemd `.socket` unit and `KillMode=process`.

A small supervisor process owns the managed OpenCode children and the listening socket. OpenChamber then restarts without dropping sessions or moving ports.

The user's instruction: "it's orchestrating/planning/managing and it should use subagents to implement/review/validate and only handle itself when it can't use a subagent somehow. it should make parallel subagents for any portions that can be broken apart."

You plan, dispatch, track and decide. **Subagents do the work:**

- **Design.** Subagents verify a design's claims against the code, research alternatives and draft revisions. The user approves designs; you don't.
- **Implement.** One subagent owns each phase and its PR. When a phase has independent parts, each part gets its own subagent in parallel, and one of them assembles the PR.
- **Review.** Before anything merges, a separate subagent with fresh context reviews every PR against the phase's steps and success criteria, its specs in `TESTING.md`, and the design sections it cites. An implementer never reviews its own work.
- **Validate.** Subagents run the targeted tests, read CI, do the manual validations (browser checks, checks on the development environment) and record the evidence in the feature package.
- **Copilot rounds.** Subagents check each Copilot finding against the code (the `review-pr-comments` skill), then fix it or explain why it's wrong. You decide what gets pushed and replied.
- **Research.** Read-only `explore` subagents answer "how does X work" questions.

**Run subagents in parallel whenever work can be split:** independent phases, independent parts of one phase, reviews and validations of different PRs, separate Copilot threads. Partition by file before any writer starts: two writers on one file clobber each other.

Do work yourself only when a subagent can't: talking to the user, making decisions, merging, or using a tool subagents lack. In OpenCode, `general` handles one task that needs judgment, `general-deep` follows one long thread, `general-wide` and `general-2wide` handle batches, and `explore*` does read-only research. Subagents may not be able to spawn subagents of their own, so every brief must be doable alone.

- developing-today/opencode#12 — finish and merge the GitHub tools plugin (PR #11) that is dogfooded in OpenChamber. Its CI has a related problem: `test.yml` needs `blacksmith-*` runners the fork doesn't have.

## History

- [#6](https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/pull/6) (2026-10-13): the desktop updater and publish target point at the fork.
- [#7](https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/pull/7)–[#11](https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/pull/11) (2026-10-14): macOS and Windows builds become opt-in, releases stay drafts until finalized, Linux llama-addon pruning, draft-release lookup. `v2.2.0` was cut right after.
- [#12](https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/pull/12), [#13](https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/pull/13) (2026-10-14): Android and every other app type take updates from the fork's releases, never npm.
- `865d470be` (2026-10-15): `projects.add` and `projects.remove`, pushed directly to `main`.
- `a16d8e79d` (2026-10-15): worktree-by-default, the Auto-create worktree switch, and the session, provider, config, MCP and skills control actions, pushed directly to `main`.
- `8f9956331` (2026-10-16): upstream `main` merged in, which raised the version to 2.3.3.
- [#17](https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/pull/17), [#20](https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/pull/20) (2026-10-16): the brace fix and the sidebar layout.
- [#23](https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/pull/23), [#24](https://github.com/developing-today/openchamber/pull/24) (2026-10-16): worktree start points and templates, and the `check:changed` fixes.

## Not verified

- **Why Actions stopped running.** I checked repo Actions permissions and run history only. I could not read org billing: `gh api /orgs/developing-today/settings/billing/actions` → HTTP 410 (endpoint moved), and the replacement needs the `admin:org` scope.
- **Whether a local `build-electron-app` succeeds** with `notarize: true` and no Apple credentials. Not run.
- **Whether the `autoCreateWorktree` switch defaults to on or off.** I read only the registry field, which declares no default.
- **Whether anyone has run a dev build of `main` since 2026-10-15.** I know only that the released and installed versions predate the work.
- **The session claims I relay without re-running them:** 348 control tests passed (`a16d8e79d`); 282/282 UI test files passed (#20); the desktop `opencode.reload` behavior; and the naming timeouts of 15 s and 20 s.
- **"No issue covers release or validation"** rests on `gh issue list -R developing-today/openchamber --state all` (8 issues) and a search for `release OR validate OR handoff`. Both returned no match.
- **"No macOS asset was ever released"** covers `v2.2.0`, the only fork release (`gh release list`).
- **The action list comes from grepping** `origin/main` `packages/web/server/lib/openchamber-control/*.js` for action names. Some actions in `actions.js` (for example `session.link`, `session.moveToWorktree`, `knowledge.*`, `memory.*`, `notify.send`, `render.page`, `browser.*`) may predate `v2.2.0`. I did not check which ones are new, apart from the commits named.

## Acceptance criteria

- A fork release newer than v2.2.0 is published on the developing-today/openchamber releases page, with its build provenance recorded on this issue.
- The user's Mac is running a build of the fork's `main`, and the install path used (given no signed macOS release exists yet) is documented on this issue.
- Each feature merged since 2026-10-14 listed under "Read first" (agent control actions, worktree-by-default, Auto-create worktree switch, sidebar layout #20, worktree start points/branch templates #23) has been used once in the running app, with the outcome written on this issue.
- Every defect found during validation is either fixed in a merged PR or filed as its own issue and linked here.

body:
A view mode that keeps the sidebar's order but draws no headers at all: no section headers (Approvals, In work, Chats, All sessions, and the rest), no project headers, no worktree headers. The sessions come one after another in exactly the order the current layout gives them (#20): the attention sections first in their configured order, then Pinned, In work, the other sections, then Chats and the projects, each in its own order.

Why: once the order itself says what needs me (attention first, then what I work on, then everything else), the headers cost a row each and the list could be read top to bottom like an inbox.

Things to settle before building:

- **Where the boundaries go.** With no headers, nothing shows where Questions ends and In work starts. Options: nothing at all, a thin divider, or a per-row mark (the section's icon in the row's slot).
- **Duplicates.** A session in a zone is also listed under its project today. Without headers the same row would show twice; the headerless mode probably lists every session once, at its first place.
- **What collapse and Show more mean.** Both hang off headers today. Probably: no collapsing, and one reveal limit for the whole list or per section.
- **Where the project shows.** Rows under a project header leave the project out; without the header every row needs its project's icon (the zone rows' `'timeline-mixed'` / `'mixed-flat'` forms already do this).
- **Tree vs List.** Whether this is a third view next to Tree and List, or a toggle that applies to both.
- **Phone.** Whether the phone sheet gets it with #18.

Code pointers: the row model draws sections in `sectionOrder` (`components/session/sidebar/sessionSidebarRowModel.ts`), and sticky headers, drag and the Done/Archive navigation all key off the header rows, so each needs a defined behavior without them.

## Acceptance criteria

- A view mode exists that renders sessions in exactly the current layout's order with no section, project, or worktree headers drawn.
- Each session appears once, at its first position in the order (no zone/project duplicates).
- Collapse and "Show more" have defined behavior in this mode (or are explicitly absent), and every row shows its project's icon since no header carries it.
- Sticky headers, drag, and Done/Archive navigation — which key off header rows today — have defined behavior without headers.
- Whether the mode is a third view or a toggle over Tree/List, and whether the phone sheet gets it, is decided and recorded on the issue.
title: Sidebar view mode without headers that keeps the section order
